units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
Showing photograph .
You are much prettier. But haven’t you got one of yourself with your little boy?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: I have. Would you prefer one of those?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Yes.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: I’ll go and get it for you, if you’ll excuse me for a moment. I have one upstairs.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: So sorry, Lady Windermere, to give you so much trouble.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Moves to door R.
No trouble at all, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Thanks so much.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: [ Exit LADY WINDERMERE R. ] You seem rather out of temper this morning, Windermere.
Why should you be?
Margaret and I get on charmingly together.
I can’t bear to see you with her. Besides, you have not told me the truth, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I have not told her the truth, you mean.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Standing C.

I sometimes wish you had. I should have been spared then the misery, the anxiety, the annoyance of the last six months. But rather than my wife should know—that the mother whom she was taught to consider as dead, the mother whom she has mourned as dead, is living—a divorced woman, going about under an assumed name, a bad woman preying upon life, as I know you now to be—rather than that, I was ready to supply you with money to pay bill after bill, extravagance after extravagance, to risk what occurred yesterday, the first quarrel I have ever had with my wife. You don’t understand what that means to me. How could you? But I tell you that the only bitter words that ever came from those sweet lips of hers were on your account, and I hate to see you next her. You sully the innocence that is in her.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Moves L.C.
And then I used to think that with all your faults you were frank and honest. You are not.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Why do you say that?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: You made me get you an invitation to my wife’s ball.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: For my daughter’s ball—yes.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: You came, and within an hour of your leaving the house you are found in a man’s rooms—you are disgraced before every one.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Goes up stage C.
Yes.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Turning round on her .
Therefore I have a right to look upon you as what you are—a worthless, vicious woman. I have the right to tell you never to enter this house, never to attempt to come near my wife—
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Coldly .
My daughter, you mean.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: You have no right to claim her as your daughter. You left her, abandoned her when she was but a child in the cradle, abandoned her for your lover, who abandoned you in turn.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Rising .
Do you count that to his credit, Lord Windermere—or to mine?
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: To his, now that I know you.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Take care—you had better be careful.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Oh, I am not going to mince words for you. I know you thoroughly.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Looks steadily at him .
I question that.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: I do know you. For twenty years of your life you lived without your child, without a thought of your child. One day you read in the papers that she had married a rich man. You saw your hideous chance. You knew that to spare her the ignominy of learning that a woman like you was her mother, I would endure anything. You began your blackmailing.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Shrugging her shoulders .
Don’t use ugly words, Windermere. They are vulgar. I saw my chance, it is true, and took it.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Yes, you took it—and spoiled it all last night by being found out.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: With a strange smile .
You are quite right, I spoiled it all last night.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: And as for your blunder in taking my wife’s fan from here and then leaving it about in Darlington’s rooms, it is unpardonable. I can’t bear the sight of it now. I shall never let my wife use it again. The thing is soiled for me. You should have kept it and not brought it back.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I think I shall keep it.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Goes up .
It’s extremely pretty.
units.name: MRS. ERLYNNE

units.text: Takes up fan .
